caption: James McNeill Whistler, Turkeys, a Venice courtyard etched in 1880 and published in the “Second Venice Set” (1886). When the edition was complete, the copper was scored with crossed lines so no more could be printed, and this proof was pulled to show that it was finished.
alt: An etching: a Venetian courtyard with balconies and hanging vines, a figure standing beside a round well-head, and a flock of turkeys pecking in the foreground. Long straight lines are scored across the whole plate, cancelling it; below, “Turkeys” is written in pencil.
bibliography: Whistler, James McNeill. Turkeys. Etched 1880, published in A Set of Twenty-Six Etchings (the “Second Venice Set”), Dowdeswell and Thibaudeau, 1886; impression from the cancelled plate, etching and drypoint, The Art Institute of Chicago, 1933.705a (Glasgow 236, Kennedy 199).
title: Turkeys
